Sign Up Login × BHP BHP Australia Graduate Program: Expression of interest Share job ad AI Job Summary Read More At BHP, we believe the best tomorrow is built through working, learning and innovating together and through this connection, building your skills for now, and the future. Come and join us in the 2028 Australia Graduate Program. Applications will open in March 2027, with the exact dates still to be confirmed. About the program The 24-month BHP Graduate Program starts in February 2028, and brings people together to learn, build capability and gain confidence for the future. You’ll build on the foundations you gained at university while developing skills that support a lifelong career. From day one, you’ll have structured onboarding, guided learning paths and support from your graduate cohort, your buddy and leaders who are passionate about helping you grow. You’ll work on meaningful projects across resources, engineering, technology, decarbonisation and safe, sustainable operations, gaining hands on experience. Graduates will rotate 2-4 times, to help build technical capabilities, working relationships with new people and leadership skills. You’ll be guided by our leaders as you work on real projects, offering accelerated learning and career path opportunities. Coursework is delivered in a combination of methods which include virtual workshops (with senior leader and graduate alumni participation), graduate workbook and a technical logbook. Plus, to continually build capabilities and professional development, you’ll have “action learning periods” where you’re given tasks to complete during your day-to-day work. This gives you the opportunity to share what you’ve learned within your designated group in discussions led by past Graduates. Join a workplace where your ideas matter, your development is prioritised and you can see the impact of your work. Many graduates say the friendships, networks and support they build during the program are among the most rewarding parts, and many of BHP’s leaders began their own careers right here. What you’ll experience as a BHP Graduate Depending on your discipline and preferred location, your role may be based in a residential community, city office, or operate on a Fly in Fly out (FIFO) roster. Western Australia’s Iron Ore assets are primarily FIFO, Queensland’s Coal operations are largely residential, and South Australia’s Copper Operations offer a mix of both. You can specify your preferred location when applying. We encourage you to consider the commitment, lifestyle, responsibilities and opportunities each working environment provides. In addition, you will: Learn how the resources sector operates by collaborating with skilled people and contributing to real projects and business challenges. Strengthen your capability by building your innovation and problem-solving abilities to help shape improvements. Learn how to communicate effectively, while building core work skills like prioritising, managing change, staying curious and developing a growth mindset. What we offer you Your graduate position can offer the beginning of a long, secure and successful career. Position We are seeking a motivated and energetic individual with the interest, capacity and commitment to developing a career in water and wastewater treatment operations. Working as part of a small and supportive team, this trainee position provides an exciting opportunity to develop practical skills and knowledge in the operation of Council’s water and wastewater treatment facilities. The successful applicant will undertake a two-year traineeship in Water Industry Treatment, gaining experience in wastewater treatment operations while completing a relevant course. Class C driver licence with an ability to operate a manual transmission. Willingness and ability to work on call in accordance with roster requirements. Health and wellbeing initiatives, including Fitness Passport member options. Meaningful work that contributes to the sustainability and liveability of our region. Provision of uniform and PPE. Sign Up Login × Jane Street Linux Engineer Share job ad AI Job Summary Read More About the Position We're looking for Linux Engineers to join the team that maintains the critical infrastructure underlying the rest of Jane Street's technology. It's a broad role, and no two Linux Engineers look exactly alike. Our work spans on-prem and cloud infrastructure, every major pillar (compute, storage, networking), and every layer of the stack from the physical hardware to workload orchestration. You should expect to work in some (but not necessarily all) of these areas, and to go genuinely deep in a few. That might mean: Building the in-house tools and systems that make up our platform, or integrating mainstream (often open-source) technologies so they feel native to our infrastructure Acting as one of the firm's Linux experts, and teaching other engineers specialist skills like systems debugging Automating our own work, because it makes us faster and more reliable (and we think it's fun) Diagnosing and resolving production issues in real time, often under time pressure Carrying out scheduled changes to the platform, like upgrades, migrations, capacity changes, and rollouts, planned meticulously and executed carefully The problem space runs from the physical to the abstract: datacenter provisioning and orchestration, kernels and drivers delivered through Nix and RPMs, production and research storage at scale, cloud that integrates cleanly with our on-prem platform, and, in partnership with our IT and Network Engineering colleagues, Linux desktops and how our hosts participate in the network. We see Linux Engineering and Software Engineering as two ends of a spectrum, and plenty of people could do either job well. Linux Engineering is likely the better fit if you treat Linux itself as your problem space: you like working close to the operating system, you want to look after production infrastructure, and you're happy spending more of your time in a consulting capacity than a typical developer would. (Compared with kernel development, the emphasis flips: you'd rarely develop the kernel itself, though targeted patches happen, and you'd spend far more time running production infrastructure.) We're hiring for both roles and are happy to advise you on which might fit best. We don't expect you to come in with deep experience; we're happy to hire smart problem-solvers and teach them what they need to know. But the job leans much more toward engineering than a traditional operations role: relentless automation instead of manual toil, and a large body of in-house technology rather than only off-the-shelf tools. You'll build systems, not just operate them. ReSource Pty Ltd is recruiting two engineering interns to develop an operational multi-camera imaging and identification station. We recover, test and remarket used IT equipment through our IT asset disposition (ITAD) operation. Your work will help our team capture better images and asset data with less manual processing. What You Will Build ReSource plans to supply a working proof of concept using a Sony A7 III camera and version 1 software. You will build on it, with freedom to improve the hardware and software within the budget and agreed maintainability requirements. Together, you will develop: The physical station: camera selection and positioning, lighting, fixtures and a practical operator workspace. The vision pipeline: device-focused images, background removal or cropping, serial-number and product-label crops, barcode reading and optical character recognition (OCR). The integrated workflow: authorised access to RazorERP (our asset-recording system), accurate asset matching, automatic posting of validated, high-confidence items, and operator review of exceptions. The operational handover: tested hardware and software, clear error recovery, source code, build and maintenance documentation, and operator training. The intended scope includes laptops, desktops, servers, phones/tablets, network equipment and components such as HDDs, SSDs, RAM, CPUs, motherboards, GPUs and PSUs. You will agree representative test items and acceptance criteria with the technical team early in the project. The design target is under 30 seconds per device from capture trigger through processing and RazorERP upload, excluding operator handling . It is a target to validate, not a reason to trade away accuracy or reliability. ReSource retains safety and production-release approval. What You Need We are looking for final-year or Masters students and recent graduates with complementary strengths. Relevant backgrounds include robotics/mechatronics, mechanical, electrical or software engineering, and computer science. Across the pair, we need practical hardware/prototyping capability and strong Python, computer-vision and API integration skills. You do not need to be an expert in everything. Show us what you have built, how you tested it and what you learned when it did not work. You can apply individually or as an existing pair. Each applicant will be assessed on their own capability and the complementary strengths of the pair. What We Train You On We will introduce you to our ITAD workflow, the supplied proof of concept, RazorERP requirements and site safety procedures. You will have two scheduled technical sessions each week , plus support as needed from our founder and internal technical team, with practical input from the ITAD operations team. Why Join ReSource Real project ownership: take a supported engineering project from prototype through testing and operational handover. Funded hardware: up to A$15,000 for the shared project's hardware , separate from wages. Most equipment will be selected and purchased for the build. A dedicated workspace: based at our Keilor East ITAD factory, primarily on-site, with flexible hours or occasional remote software work by agreement. Portfolio evidence: an approved demonstration, photographs and technical case study, with confidential information removed. Potential beyond summer: this could be one of several combined AI and hardware projects as ReSource looks to improve efficiency and data collection. Strong performers may have opportunities for further paid work or a graduate role, depending on business needs. The intended commitment is 12 weeks full-time within the November-February summer window, allowing for the Christmas shutdown. University course credit, if sought, is subject to university approval. How To Apply Send your CV and a short practical project example or portfolio to [email protected] . Beyond orientation, our trading floor serves as an unlimited source of discussion for learning and development.
